title: Surrey And White Rock Families Get Halloween Diwali Safety Checklist
excerpt: Halloween falls on October 31 and Diwali on November 8. Surrey's fireworks fines run to $50,000, bylaw officers will patrol with police, and police have a line-by-line trick-or-treat checklist for families.
body:
• Halloween is Saturday, October 31 and Diwali is Sunday, November 8 in Surrey — and fireworks are effectively banned for residents without federal certification and a Surrey Fire Service permit.
  • Fireworks fines in Surrey run from $400 to $50,000, each day counts as a separate offence, and bylaw officers will patrol with police in high-activity areas.
  • Report illegal fireworks to Surrey Bylaws at 604-591-4370. Call 9-1-1 only in an emergency.
  • For trick-or-treaters: bright costumes with reflective tape, a flashlight or glow stick, sidewalks and crosswalks only, and no candy eaten until an adult has checked it.

Surrey and White Rock families are heading into two big nights a week apart — Halloween on October 31 and Diwali on November 8 — and the City of Surrey has put its safety rules out early. The headline rule is about fireworks: in Surrey, they are prohibited for almost everyone, on both nights. The full notice is on the City of Surrey website.

The fireworks rules, exactly as written

Under the Surrey Fireworks Regulation Bylaw No. 4200, the sale, purchase and use of fireworks are not permitted in Surrey without two things together: federal certification, and a valid permit from the Surrey Fire Service. Possession of fireworks by anyone under 18 is prohibited. Setting off fireworks on public property, including school grounds, is also prohibited, Surrey Schools confirms.

The penalties are steep. Violators face a minimum fine of $400 and a maximum of $50,000, and each day an offence occurs is a separate violation. Surrey raised the fines in 2024, from a $100 minimum and $5,000 maximum. Leading up to Halloween and on Diwali day, bylaw officers will be deployed in high-activity areas across Surrey working with police — responding to reports, gathering evidence and issuing tickets. If you see fireworks being discharged illegally, call Surrey Bylaws at 604-591-4370. Keep 9-1-1 for emergencies only. The City says unauthorised fireworks can cause injuries and fires, and distress vulnerable residents and animals.

Trick-or-treating: the Surrey Police checklist

The Surrey Police Service safety reminders are specific, and worth following line by line:

  • Make children visible: bright costumes, reflective tape on coats, and a flashlight or glow stick.
  • Walk on sidewalks and cross only at crosswalks or intersections. Do not run between parked cars or take shortcuts through alleys.
  • Younger children go with an adult; older children go in groups, in well-lit areas. Plan the route in advance and set a return time.
  • Never enter a stranger's home for treats, and do not eat candy until an adult has checked it. Discard anything not in its original packaging or that looks tampered with — Surrey Schools adds: check for choking hazards and peanut treats for children with allergies.
  • Fake weapons must look obviously fake. Surrey Schools also advises face paint instead of masks that can block vision, and LED candles in jack-o'-lanterns instead of real flames.

Homeowners: turn on exterior lighting, keep steps and pathways lit and clear, and keep pets indoors when trick-or-treaters arrive. Drivers should slow down in residential areas, expect children to move unpredictably, put the phone away, and plan a designated driver, rideshare, cab or transit ride home from any Halloween party. Suspicious activity goes to the Surrey Police non-emergency line at 604-599-0502.

For Diwali at home

The same fireworks bylaw applies on Diwali — there is no festival exception in Surrey without the certification and permit above, and enforcement is planned for Diwali day itself. Families marking the festival of lights at home should treat candles and diyas with the same care Surrey Schools advises for pumpkins: keep flames away from curtains and decorations, never leave them unattended, and keep pets inside and away from doors as visitors arrive. Celebrate with lights, not unauthorised fireworks, and both neighbourhoods — Surrey and White Rock — get the festival without the fines, fires or frightened animals.

items: No fireworks without federal certification AND a Surrey Fire Service permit (Bylaw No. 4200)
Fireworks fines: $400 minimum to $50,000 maximum; each day is a separate offence
No fireworks on public property, including school grounds
Report illegal fireworks: Surrey Bylaws 604-591-4370 (9-1-1 emergencies only)
Children visible: reflective tape, flashlight or glow stick; cross only at crosswalks
No candy until an adult checks it; discard unpackaged or tampered items
